attacks.claim: The plan never shows the send pipeline is isolated from the site. The stated cause of outages is WP-cron sending competing with site traffic, yet Ghost is placed on a single 4 vCPU/8 GB box with MySQL co-located, so web, DB, email jobs and backups still share one failure domain with no stated resource isolation or single-node failover.
attacks.evidence: "MySQL 8 on the same box, nightly encrypted dumps" and "Ghost 5.x ... via the official Docker image on a new 4 vCPU / 8 GB VPS"

attacks.claim: The 30-day read-only WordPress rollback is not credible as written: once Ghost is live and taking signups and sends, rolling back to MailPoet requires re-importing new members and sends made during the window, and there is no described sync or reconciliation of Ghost-side unsubscribes/bounces back to MailPoet, risking re-mailing opted-out readers.
attacks.evidence: "rollback = repoint DNS and re-enable MailPoet sending, with any new Ghost signups exported and re-imported to MailPoet." (no mention of unsubscribes, bounces or complaints made in Ghost)

attacks.claim: The suppression rule only covers unsubscribed and bounced addresses from MailPoet, but complaints (spam reports) are not mentioned, and the paid-member matching has 37 unresolved mismatches with no defined handling for members who cannot be matched, so billing and access state for those members is undefined at cutover.
attacks.evidence: "Unsubscribed and bounced addresses are imported as suppressed" and "37 members with mismatched emails were identified in a dry run and will be resolved by hand before cutover."

attacks.claim: Load-bearing cost and deliverability claims are unprototyped: the $90/mo Mailgun estimate is not derived, and the plan states the sender reputation and 2% bounce / 0.1% complaint gate without any warm-up volume plan. Moving 46k recipients from an existing sending domain/IP to a new Mailgun domain carries real inbox-placement risk that the gate does not account for.
attacks.evidence: "Estimated $90/mo at our volume (46k x ~4.3 sends/month)." and "Mailgun domain warm-up (SPF/DKIM/DMARC)" (warm-up only in week 2, no volume ramp)

attacks.claim: The stated run cost does not reconcile: $140 VPS+Mailgun+storage is claimed, but $48 VPS + $90 Mailgun is $138 before storage and backups, and the constraint is <= $300 so headroom is not stated against paid-member Stripe fees or Ghost-hosted-alternative comparison.
attacks.evidence: "Total run cost: ~$140/mo VPS + Mailgun + storage, vs $95/mo today."

attacks.claim: The 46k-subscriber, 4.3-sends/month figure is used for Mailgun cost but the plan does not address sending throughput or batching against Mailgun rate limits during the 2-hour seed-then-remainder send, nor the 8 GB RAM headroom for a 46k-recipient job on the same host as MySQL.
attacks.evidence: "the remainder sends 2 hours later" and "4 vCPU / 8 GB VPS"

attacks.claim: Migrating MailPoet consent records and IP addresses into a new system requires the plan to show lawful basis and retention limits for the consent IPs and that the consent source is verifiable for each address; the plan keeps IPs for 30-day dumps and object storage with no retention or deletion policy for the historical consent data.
attacks.evidence: "consent source/IP where recorded" and "nightly encrypted dumps to object storage (30-day retention)"

attacks.claim: Subscriber PII (emails, IPs, consent records) is copied to object storage, a Mailgun account and a Postmark test account without any stated data-processing agreement or access control for the backup bucket.
attacks.evidence: "nightly encrypted dumps to object storage" and "Postmark Broadcasts"

attacks.claim: The exit rehearsal depends on Mailgun for production sending and Postmark for the rehearsal; the 50-address Postmark test does not prove the production sender can be swapped at 46k scale, so the stated exit is weaker than presented.
attacks.evidence: "In week 2 we rehearse this end to end with a 50-address internal list through Postmark Broadcasts"

attacks.claim: Cutover on a Tuesday leaves a 2-day window before the Thursday send, but the timeline has week 3 final Thursday MailPoet send and week 4 cutover, so the editors have one week of Ghost-only work with no defined content freeze, risking missed or duplicated issues.
attacks.evidence: "Cutover Tuesday (send day is Thursday), giving 2 days to fix issues before the first Ghost send."

attacks.claim: Scope relies on a 0.5 FTE developer for a 4-week build covering VPS, Ghost, WP export with 41 manual shortcode fixes, theme port, routes, Stripe import and Mailgun setup, with no contingency or named owner for the Ghost theme port.
attacks.evidence: "Owner: dev (0.5 FTE) + managing editor | 4 weeks"

attacks.claim: Success measure for outages is set for the first quarter after cutover but there is no alerting or monitoring defined for send-day failures on the new stack.
attacks.evidence: "Zero send-day outages over the first quarter." (ABSENT: monitoring/alerting for sends)

attacks.claim: Rollback path is not viable as written: after cutover, Ghost signups/members/Stripe subscriptions accrue on the new system, and the rollback only re-exports new signups to MailPoet. Paid member state and Stripe webhook targets would be split across two systems with no defined reconciliation, and the 30-day window has no stated cutover-of-payments reversal.
attacks.evidence: "rollback = repoint DNS and re-enable MailPoet sending, with any new Ghost signups exported and re-imported to MailPoet."

attacks.claim: Schedule is internally inconsistent: the cutover is Tuesday of week 4 but the Stripe import dry run and reconciliation are in week 3, and the final MailPoet send is in week 3 Thursday; the 37 mismatched paid members are said to be resolved 'by hand before cutover' with no owner or deadline, and the DNS TTL change is 'one week before cutover' which lands in week 3 while the Stripe/member data is still being reconciled.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: Stripe import dry run, reconciliation, editor training; final Thursday send on MailPoet." / "37 members with mismatched emails ... will be resolved by hand before cutover."

attacks.claim: Cutover timing creates a data gap: MailPoet's final send is week 3 Thursday, but subscriber state changes (unsubscribes, bounces, new signups) between the last import snapshot and DNS flip are not addressed, so the production import may re-mail or miss opt-outs that occurred after the export.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no delta-sync or freeze procedure between final MailPoet export and Ghost production import; "Unsubscribed and bounced addresses are imported as suppressed" assumes a snapshot is current at cutover.

attacks.claim: The cost claim is not reconciled: the stated total is ~$140/mo VPS+Mailgun+storage, but $48 VPS + $90 Mailgun already equals $138 before storage; the 'vs $95/mo today' comparison and the Mailgun estimate are not shown with any pricing basis or send-volume math beyond 46k x 4.3.
attacks.evidence: "Total run cost: ~$140/mo VPS + Mailgun + storage, vs $95/mo today." / "Estimated $90/mo at our volume (46k x ~4.3 sends/month)."

attacks.claim: The plan replaces the failing component (single VPS sending during shared PHP load) with a Ghost box that is again a single VPS running app, MySQL, and backups on one host with no stated failover, monitoring, or send-time load test, so the stated success measure of zero send-day outages is not supported by any mechanism addressing the 4 prior outage causes.
attacks.evidence: "MySQL 8 on the same box" / ABSENT: no load test at 46k recipients, no alerting, no failover, and no root-cause analysis of the Feb/Apr/Jun/Sep outages.

attacks.claim: Backups are described as nightly dumps only, meaning up to ~24h of member/consent/payment changes can be lost on host failure, and the dump restore is never tested end-to-end; only the Ghost export round-trip is rehearsed, which is not a full DB restore.
attacks.evidence: "nightly encrypted dumps to object storage (30-day retention)" / "we restore one export into a scratch Ghost instance in week 2"

attacks.claim: Transferring subscriber consent records and IP addresses to a new US-based processor (Mailgun) and Stripe-linked data without a stated data-processing review, lawful-basis note, or privacy notice update; consent IPs are migrated as-is with no retention policy for them.
attacks.evidence: "Export MailPoet subscribers with status, list membership, subscribe date, and consent source/IP where recorded." / ABSENT: no DPA, privacy notice update, or retention limit for consent IPs.

attacks.claim: Consent IP and member data are included in weekly exports stored alongside DB dumps in object storage with no encryption-at-rest or access-control detail for the export files themselves.
attacks.evidence: "Ghost's members CSV export and JSON content export are scheduled weekly (cron, stored with the DB dumps)"

attacks.claim: Exit path depends on Postmark for the rehearsal but the plan names Mailgun as primary with no tested second provider in production; the rehearsal uses a different vendor than the one the plan actually relies on.
attacks.evidence: "through Postmark Broadcasts (export -> import -> send -> unsubscribe link writes back via Ghost members API)"

attacks.claim: The 2-hour delayed remainder send after a seeded first send adds reader-facing lateness and an extra manual gate; the thresholds (bounce <2%, complaint <0.1%) are not tied to any baseline from MailPoet.
attacks.evidence: "the remainder sends 2 hours later if bounce rate < 2% and complaint rate < 0.1%"

attacks.claim: Seed segment of 2,000 out of 46,000 plus 2-hour delay doesn't address the 10x growth or the send-time concurrency of Ghost's worker queue on a 4 vCPU box; no throughput figure is given.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no measured Ghost send throughput or queue-time estimate for 46,000 recipients.

attacks.claim: Wholesale 41 shortcode fixes by script and a manual 37-member Stripe reconciliation are one-off steps with no test or audit trail beyond the dry run.
attacks.evidence: "41 posts with embedded shortcodes fixed by script"

attacks.claim: Success measure 'zero send-day outages over the first quarter' is unfalsifiable as a gate criterion for a 4-week build and does not define what happens if an outage occurs post-cutover.
attacks.evidence: "Zero send-day outages over the first quarter."

attacks.claim: The plan has no delta sync of unsubscribes and bounces from MailPoet between the export snapshot and cutover, and none from Ghost back to MailPoet on rollback. Opted-out people could be re-mailed, which is an irreversible consent and legal violation.
attacks.evidence: "Rollback = repoint DNS and re-enable MailPoet sending, with any new Ghost signups exported and re-imported to MailPoet." ABSENT: unsubscribe/bounce delta sync in either direction.

attacks.claim: Paid-member cutover is underspecified. The plan does not say which system owns entitlements and billing during the switch, how Stripe webhooks are repointed, or how the old membership and Stripe plugins are shut off. This risks double subscriptions or dropped cancellations and failed-payment events.
attacks.evidence: "Paid members are matched to Stripe customers by Stripe customer ID... using Ghost's Stripe import; 37 members with mismatched emails... will be resolved by hand before cutover." ABSENT: webhook endpoint change, plugin decommission, subscription-ownership handoff.

attacks.claim: The rollback path breaks once Ghost has sent. Re-enabling MailPoet against a list that is 30 days stale, with WordPress still live read-only, creates dual-send and divergence risk. No rollback criteria or trigger are defined for after the first Ghost send.
attacks.evidence: "WordPress stays running read-only on the old VPS for 30 days; rollback = repoint DNS and re-enable MailPoet sending"

attacks.claim: Secrets handling and dump-encryption key management are not specified. Member exports with consent IPs sit in the same object storage as the dumps, with no access-control or key-rotation plan.
attacks.evidence: "nightly encrypted dumps to object storage (30-day retention)" and "stored with the DB dumps". ABSENT: key custody, bucket access policy, Stripe/Mailgun key storage, admin-interface hardening.

attacks.claim: Personal data, including consent IP addresses, is copied to Mailgun, object storage, and staging with no minimization or retention policy. The plan also does not address whether consent records remain valid across the change of platform and processor.
attacks.evidence: "consent source/IP where recorded"; "Mailgun only receives per-send recipient batches". ABSENT: retention period for IPs, Mailgun DPA/transfer basis, consent-carryover basis.

attacks.claim: Mailgun is the sole bulk sender. The exit rehearsal uses 50 addresses through a different provider, and the Ghost writeback from that provider is unverified, so the exit cost is not evidenced at real volume.
attacks.evidence: "rehearse this end to end with a 50-address internal list through Postmark Broadcasts... unsubscribe link writes back via Ghost members API"

attacks.claim: Nothing tests the 46k-recipient send path or the inbound Mailgun event volume (about 200k sends/month, plus delivery and bounce webhooks) on a single 4 vCPU / 8 GB box that also runs MySQL. No load test appears in the timeline.
attacks.evidence: "46k x ~4.3 sends/month"; "4 vCPU / 8 GB VPS ($48/mo"; timeline has no load-test step.

attacks.claim: The cost math is incomplete. The $90 Mailgun figure is unsourced, storage is unquantified, and the comparison to today's $95 omits the Postmark rehearsal and staging costs.
attacks.evidence: "Estimated $90/mo at our volume"; "~$140/mo VPS + Mailgun + storage, vs $95/mo today"

attacks.claim: The architecture repeats the single-VPS, co-located-database setup that caused four send-day outages. Nightly dumps allow up to 24 hours of lost unsubscribes and signups on restore, and no HA, monitoring, or alerting is defined.
attacks.evidence: "MySQL 8 on the same box, nightly encrypted dumps"; "Zero send-day outages over the first quarter." ABSENT: alerting, RPO/RTO, failover.

attacks.claim: Deliverability risk is under-planned. Domain warm-up runs about two weeks, then a 46k send follows, with an auto-proceed gate that reads complaint and bounce rates only 2 hours after the seed send.
attacks.evidence: "Mailgun domain warm-up (SPF/DKIM/DMARC)" in week 2; "remainder sends 2 hours later if bounce rate < 2% and complaint rate < 0.1%"

attacks.claim: Mailgun reputation and suppression state do not transfer on exit. The plan does not address how sender reputation survives a provider switch.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: reputation or suppression-list transfer plan for Mailgun exit.

attacks.claim: URL preservation is load-bearing but unprototyped. The crawl covers only 2,000 of 6,812 posts, the shortcode fix is an untested script, and no failure threshold is set for the rest.
attacks.evidence: "URL structure kept identical (/YYYY/MM/slug/) via Ghost routes.yaml"; "A crawl of the 2,000 most-visited URLs from analytics must return 200/301"

attacks.claim: The theme port has no visual or mobile regression acceptance criteria, and the signup and paywall rendering is not verified.
attacks.evidence: "theme port" in week 2; ABSENT: visual QA criteria.

attacks.claim: Success measures cover only ops and time savings. No reader-facing metrics such as open rate, deliverability, or churn are defined to show the migration serves readers.
attacks.evidence: "Zero send-day outages"; "Member reconciliation time... < 30 min/month."

attacks.claim: Editors must learn Ghost in week 3, the same week as the final MailPoet send, which squeezes training and the send.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: Stripe import dry run, reconciliation, editor training; final Thursday send on MailPoet."

attacks.claim: The theme port has no accessibility acceptance criteria for keyboard navigation, contrast, or screen readers.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: accessibility criteria in the theme-port scope.

attacks.claim: Scope exceeds the staffing. Theme port, exporters, shortcode script, Stripe migration, Mailgun warm-up, backups, and training fit into four weeks at 0.5 FTE, and the manual member-resolution work has no named owner.
attacks.evidence: "Owner: dev (0.5 FTE) + managing editor | 4 weeks"; "37 members... will be resolved by hand before cutover"

attacks.claim: The cutover date depends on unresolved manual work and dry-run results with no go/no-go criteria, so the schedule is not gated on completion.
attacks.evidence: "Cutover target: Tuesday after week 3 send"; ABSENT: go/no-go checklist.
